eyebrow: A field manual for AI agent harness engineering
title: Harness Patterns
lede: Software design patterns are tried-and-tested ways to solve common problems in code. This book takes every pattern in the classic catalog and shows where it fits when you build an AI agent system for a business. Each one comes with an everyday comparison, a picture, and a note on how large companies use it. The language is kept simple, and every technical word is explained when it first appears.

sections.heading: First, what is an agent harness?
paragraphs: An AI model on its own only reads text and writes text. An agent is a model that can also do things: look something up, edit a file, send a message, then decide what to do next. The harness is all the software around the model that makes this possible and safe. It sends the conversation to the model, runs the tools the model asks for, remembers what happened, checks permissions, and shows the results to people.
Think of the model as a skilled pilot and the harness as the aircraft, the control tower and the airport rules. The pilot makes the decisions, but nothing flies safely without everything around them.

sections.heading: The harness at a glance
paragraphs: The chapters follow the main parts of a harness. Find the part you are building, then read that chapter.

sections.heading: How to read a diagram
paragraphs: Shapes and colours mean the same thing on every page. A box with an orange outline is the pattern itself: the piece you would write. Orange arrows show the main path. Dashed arrows show something optional, delayed, or going back the other way.
